why.shell.b_mark_pnt_tables.101: Guess Who Hard (7 rounds) with the new test prices (+2500 per round, −1000 per mistake, −100 per second). The current table gives an average player 34 and a strong one 63, and 68 % of novice attempts end at raw 0 (mark 1 %): a mistake costs 25 s and the base is small, so the lower half of the players sits on the floor. New marks: novice 25, average 50, strong 81, expert 93; raw 0 only below θ ≈ 10.
why.ant_head_wnd: Test-only keys (sp_* of ant_head_wnd, and ant_head_sp_show_results so that the results sheet items add up to the total). A mistake costs 1000 instead of 2500 (10 s instead of 25 s): the luck of mistakes was 75–83 % of a player's attempt-to-attempt variance in Guess Who. A solved round is worth 2500 instead of 1700, so the raw score no longer clamps at 0 for novices (68 % → 1 % of attempts). Guessing still does not pay: clicking the objects of the clue's colour at random costs ≈ 2.5 mistakes per round = 25 s, against ≈ 7 s of careful search for an average player. Effect on the Guess Who mark: SEM 13.2 → 10.0 points, retest r 0.68 → 0.79.

why.MG_antenna_head_easy.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: easy — novice 60–75 % of games, average ≥ 95 %): up 4400 → 3700 = 78 s for the 7 rounds at no wrong tap (11.2 s a round; 58 s with one wrong tap; was 66 s). Novice 47 → 69 %, average 95 → 99 %, strong 100 %; games for the 3 steps: novice 6 → 4, average 3. Real play logs agree (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md). Only the threshold changes; the rounds, the features and the prices are as before (owner, 3.6: on Hard two features are easier to follow than four on Easy — leave it for now; the idea of a fix is in docs/games/guess_who.md §10). Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18; with the 3.6 thresholds the average model player opens all 12 games in 17–23 trainings and the novice in 31–41 (was 23–30 and 63–86; tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py).
why.MG_antenna_head_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 10500 → 7500 = 107 s for the 10 rounds at no wrong tap (10.7 s a round; 75 s with one wrong tap, 43 s with two; was 64 s). Novice 4 → 44 %, average 54 → 91 %, strong 100 %; games for the 5 steps: novice 131 → 11, average 9 → 5. Weak results (< 3000): novice 10 %, average 0 %. In real play logs a Medium round is slower than a round of the test layout, where the model expects the opposite (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md). Only the threshold changes (see MG_antenna_head_easy).
why.MG_antenna_head_hard.level_up_param: Re-fit to the new hard prices and to the owner's target (average 20-30 %). up 26500 = 110 s for the 15 rounds at no wrong tap (7.3 s a round; 90 s with two wrong taps): average 25 %, strong 100 %, novice 0 %; weak games (< 10600): average 0 %, novice 21 %. Before (up 18000 at the old prices): average 1 %, strong 77 %, and the average player never left hard. 39 games for the 10 steps of the average player, 10 for the strong one. The strong target (75-90 %) cannot be met together with the average one: the model strong player is twice as fast (3.5 s a round against 7.4 s), about 3 standard deviations above the average; up 31000 would give strong 80 % and average 0 %. Medium stays at 10500 (average 54 %, novice 4 %, strong 98 %).
why.ant_head_wnd.points_good_move_arr: Training prices only (the test reads sp_*; add the keys to the existing ant_head_wnd object, the sp_* keys stay). Hard paid less than medium: the model average player (tools/analysis/train_balance_guess_who.mjs, real round generator; profiles = the doc's test-layout assumptions 12.4 / 7.3 / 3.5 s a round and 2 / 1 / 0.2 wrong taps per 7 rounds) scored 3437 / 10120 / 9301 on easy / medium / hard, because on hard the time (111 s x 100) and the wrong taps (2.1 x 2500) took 64 % of the 25500 gross. A hard round is now worth 2500 (the test price since 3.2.0) instead of 1700: gross 37500, the average player keeps 24317 (x2.4 of medium), novice 14421, strong 31893. A slow but accurate hard game (twice the average time, no wrong tap) gives 15300 — above the same player's typical medium game (10120); before it gave 3300.
why.ant_head_wnd.points_wrong_move_arr: Hard: -2500 -> -1000 per wrong tap, as in the test since 3.2.0. A hard round has 10.5 look-alikes (objects that fail one asked feature; easy 1.2, medium 3.5), so wrong taps are part of normal play there (average 2.1 a game against 0.4 on medium); at -2500 they took 21 % of the gross and gave 57-70 % of the score variance (luck). Easy and medium keep their prices.
why.ant_head_wnd.time_penalty_arr: Easy: -120 -> -60 per second. At -120 a round (1200) was eaten in 10 s while the model novice needs 9.2 s a round and the average 5.7 s: novice mean 928 of 8400, a game at 1.5 x the average time scored 1200. At -60 a round pays for 20 s (medium 21 s, hard 25 s): novice 4110, average 5816, strong 7180. Medium (-70) and hard (-100) stay.
why.ant_head_show_results.i1_points_arr: The items of the training results sheet must show the same prices as ant_head_wnd (the total comes from ant_head_wnd): round 1200 / 1500 / 2500.
